title: Introduce audit-visibility-filter and KMS usage mediator
author: Anika Shah
release_notes: Adds audit visibility filtering and a mediator that routes KMS requests based on tenant residency claims. Backwards compatible; feature-gated behind `audit_visibility_filter` flag. Includes migration tool to backfill audit visibility preferences for existing tenants.
description: Motivation: Customers with mixed residency requirements asked for finer-grained control over which audit attributes are visible to downstream systems and operators, and tighter guarantees that KMS calls are routed only to approved region-scoped key providers. This PR introduces two cooperating pieces: 1) an audit-visibility-filter service that evaluates RBAC v2 attributes (role, tenant-residency, operator-scope) and redacts or masks audit fields before events are written or forwarded; 2) a KMS usage mediator that enforces residency routing heuristics and produces an append-only 'KMS usage proof' header consumed by the audit pipeline. Scope: - Internal runtime changes to attach residency assertions to requests and to consult visibility rules prior to audit emission. - New policy schema (rbacv2 visibility rules) and a small migration to translate existing tenant metadata to default visibility profiles. - Integration tests covering cross-region failure modes and proof header reconstruction. Compatibility: Default behavior remains unchanged; both features are behind the feature-flag audit_visibility_filter and kms_usage_mediator. Rollout plan: - Canary rollout to staging and a single enterprise tenant for 48h. - Monitor audit-delivery-rate and KMS latency. - After signoff, enable for additional tenants via a gradual Linear-backed rollout. Key decisions: - Visibility rules are expressed as attribute-based allow/deny predicates (not per-operator whitelists) to avoid brittle lists across orgs. - Proof header is HMAC-signed using a short-lived mediator key to avoid leaking CMK material. Security review notes: KMS mediator never materializes customer keys; it only selects an endpoint and emits signed attestations. Migration: A script is included to create visibility profiles for tenants that opt-in to stricter masking. See docs/operations/audit-visibility-migration.md for details. Tests: Unit coverage for policy eval, integration test that simulates a routed KMS failure and verifies audit fallback path. The description below contains a compact summary of changes, commits, and review thread.

review_comments: Miguel Torres (Reviewer): This is a big surface area change — please confirm we have no path that leaks unredacted PII to external sinks. Author reply: Tests added that exercise redaction paths; visibility_evaluator runs at the last writer hop before any external forwarders.

Priya Desai (Security): How are mediator keys rotated and who can access them? Author reply: Mediator keys are stored in the cluster KMS with operator-only ACL; rotation is automated via the key-manager job documented in ops/keys.md. We added rotation unit tests and a manual rotation playbook.

Elliot Moore (SRE): Concern about added latency on hot path. Author reply: Evaluator caches policy decisions for 10s and the mediator does a best-effort async proof signing with bounded backpressure; measured P50 increase is +3ms in canary in us-west-2.
Miguel Torres: Please add a feature-flag gate to charts. Author reply: Added feature flag gates and helm values in charts templates; included in this PR.
Priya Desai: Approve after key rotation doc update. Author reply: Updated docs and re-requested review; Priya approved on re-run.
Elliot Moore: CI flaked on integration test once; reran and green. Author reply: Fixed flakiness by increasing simulated timeout in test harness.
Automated code review (LGTM-bot): No lints of severity high; minor comments inline.

migration_instructions: Run api/migrations/20251112_add_visibility_profiles.sql against the control plane DB using the migration tool `dbmigrate`. For tenants that require strict masking set visibility_profile = 'strict' using the admin API. A migration helper script is included at scripts/backfill_visibility.sh.
observability_changes: New metrics: audit_visibility_eval_latency_ms, audit_events_masked_total, kms_mediator_route_latency_ms, kms_proof_header_signed_total. Added dashboard: Security / Audit Visibility (per-tenant breakdown). Alerts: increased error budget sensitivity during rollout (SEV2 if audit_delivery_failure_rate > 0.5% for 15m).
security_considerations: Mediator never exports CMK material. Proof header is HMAC-SHA256 signed with mediator key; validators verify signature and TTL. Audit-visibility rules are applied server-side; operator consoles only receive redacted payloads unless granted visibility via RBAC attribute. We added a third-party security review tag and updated the threat model.
rollback_plan: Feature flags can be turned off to restore previous behaviour. To rollback KMS mediator selection entirely set kms_usage_mediator=false and restart mediator deployments; for audit visibility disable audit_visibility_filter and revert canary tenants via admin API. DB migration is additive; no destructive changes — rollback unnecessary for SQL migration but a backfill can be undone by restoring from a pre-migration snapshot if exact state is required.
notes: This PR was coordinated with the enterprise onboarding team for tenant 'eu-finance-01' which acted as the canary customer. The mediator's telemetry will be monitored for 72h post-merge and the on-call rotation updated to include the security SME for the first 7 days.
